For L>r_c the quadratic P(q)=c²Lq²−2cq−cL−1 has one positive root; P(L)=Q(L)>0 gives q<L, and substitution gives Q(q)=(2cq+1)(q/L−1)<0. The positive root is exactly the stated radical. The quadratic makes c(1−cq²)=−(1+2cq)/L, so the gap is nonnegative and its exact contact set on [0,L] is {q,L}. Joining f on [0,q] to ell yields a differentiable concave majorant; Jensen bounds all Borel laws, and the point mass or the stated two-atom law attains the bound, proving it is the least concave majorant. For a mean below q a tangent of this majorant meets it only at the mean by strict curvature on [0,q] and the strictly lower slope beyond q. For m≥q integrating the exact tangent gap forces support {q,L} and the mean fixes the weights, reducing to the appropriate point mass at each endpoint.
